verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch — 13:00, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY I’d treat Rey Cortiço at lunch as a check-first situation. It’s the best available option, but the wind angle is pretty poor and the confidence is low, so it could get messy quickly. I’ll be checking Surfline cams and MEO Beachcam before leaving—if they don’t look a lot better than expected, I’d skip it and save the drive.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a fun-sized north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: not captured, energy not captured, 9 s period, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at low tide can still work on Belgas if the sandbars are lined up, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.
